title: Manus acquisition and hiring practices for foreign-founded and redomiciled start-ups
asked: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre asked what share of Manus's core workforce were Singapore citizens before its acquisition, whether the deal guarantees local headcount retention or technology transfer, and how MOM ensures foreign-founded start-ups benefiting from Singapore's business environment transfer skills to local workers.
response: Dr Koh Poh Koon said the Manus acquisition is a commercial agreement between the parties involved and that MOM does not intervene in such agreements. He said the Government does not disclose individual companies' workforce demographics, and that all foreign companies operating in Singapore are expected to comply with Singapore's manpower laws and fair hiring practices. He pointed to EDB's Enterprise Compute Initiative, which partners cloud providers such as Microsoft to help Singapore-based companies build dedicated local AI teams, and to reskilling and upskilling support from Workforce Singapore and SkillsFuture Singapore. On redomiciled companies, he said they are not treated differently on hiring practices and that the laws protect workers' rights in hiring and retrenchment.
